one_line: Sixty plots, one standpipe, and a hosepipe argument every July.
monitor_rationale: reads the standpipe meter this season; four months, then somebody else does

ladder.label: hose-hours
ladder.text: The hose is off between ten in the morning and six in the evening.

shared.label: site-buys
shared.text: Anything bought out of the plot fees is agreed before it is bought.

access.label: one-key
access.text: Every plotholder holds a gate key.

inner_a.label: tunnel-vented
inner_a.text: The polytunnel is vented before nine on any day forecast over twenty-five.

inner_b.label: tunnel-trays
inner_b.text: Seed trays in the tunnel carry a plot number and a sowing date.

clash_a.label: no-bare-soil
clash_a.text: A bed is not left bare over winter.

clash_b.label: dig-in-autumn
clash_b.text: Heavy clay beds are turned in autumn and left to the frost.

extra.label: paths-cut
extra.text: The grass path beside your plot is yours to cut.

policy.root: We decide by consent: one reasoned objection stops a thing, and saying nothing is not an objection. Changing something we have called a principle takes the site, and anything we cannot undo is not decided by silence.
policy.inner: Whoever runs the propagation benches decides the polytunnel.
policy.unheld: The car park is decided by whoever holds it.
policy.ladder: The first time we ask. The second time the site asks together. The third time the answer is no.
policy.inner_amended: Two of us have to object before a polytunnel thing stops.

inner_proposal.text: fit an automatic vent opener and drop the before-nine rule
inner_proposal.because: an opener vents on temperature, which is what the rule was reaching for

inner_objection: the openers stick in the first hot week every year and nobody notices until the seedlings have gone

unheld_proposal.text: mark out bays and put a barrier on the car park

monitor_watch.about: the standpipe ran at two in the afternoon
monitor_watch.because: the meter shows a draw between ten and six and the rule names those hours
monitor_watch.dismissal: these two do not really conflict

ladder_subject.about: watering in the middle of the day
ladder_subject.first: water the new fruit trees at midday through the dry spell
ladder_subject.second: water the squash bed at midday because it wilted
ladder_subject.third: water the whole top row at midday every day this week
ladder_subject.because: midday water is mostly lost to the air and the standpipe pressure is shared with everyone above the bend
ladder_subject.ruling_1: the trees were newly in and we left it there
ladder_subject.ruling_2: the site agreed one more, then no more

other_subject.about: burning green waste on the site
other_subject.text: burn the green waste heap at the bottom of the site

clash.text: leave the two clay beds turned and bare from October so the frost can work on them
clash.because_a: bare soil over winter is soil off the site by March
clash.because_b: clay that is not frosted is clay nobody can work in spring
clash.carried: the two beds are the only heavy clay on the site and they are at the bottom where the run-off is caught; revisit when the swale is dug

amend_convention.text: cut every path with the site mower on one Saturday a month
amend_convention.because: half the paths are never cut and the mower is already here

amend_principle.text: allow a bed to be left bare if it is sheeted
amend_principle.because: a sheet holds the soil, which is the thing the rule is actually about

irreversible.text: take out the three dead apples and put plots on that corner

silence.about: who opens the gate on a Sunday morning
silence.rationale: somebody is always there by eight and writing a rota would make the first person late instead of early
silence.proposal: put a Sunday gate rota on the noticeboard

panel.rationale: three people to look at the winter cover rule for a month
